link.note: Named 'my beloved wife Keturah' in Thomas Lamoreaux's will and in the 1812 Luzerne deed (confirmed). Her parentage (John Tuthill & Temperance Smith) is probable, about 80%: the only printed statement of it, Alva Tuttle (1968), comes from the family contributor Lotta (Tuthill) Vail; supporting it are the 1752 Smithtown marriage of John and Temperance (now proved from the church register), her birth at Woodbury Clove where her Smith uncles and the Tuthills lived, the family names, and DAR sheets placing the marriage in Orange County about 1770.

summary: Orange County-born wife of Ensign Thomas Lamoreaux and the link between the Pennsylvania lines and the colonial Long Island Tuthills and Smiths; John's 6th-great-grandmother.
bio:
Keturah Tuttle, or Tuthill, was born in December 1755 at Woodbury Clove in Orange County, New York. She was probably a daughter of John Tuthill (about 1730 to about 1770) and Temperance Smith, whose other children were the twins James and John, born 1753, the twins Ezekiel and William, born about 1754, Samuel and Daniel. Her parents had been married at Smithtown on Long Island in November 1752. Keturah's own children James, Temperance and Keturah carry the names of that family, and she was evidently named for her aunt Keturah Smith. Her mother Temperance was a daughter of James Smith and Jerusha Topping, and Temperance's brothers Captain Francis Smith and Captain Austin Smith had settled at Woodbury Clove some twenty years before the Revolution; Austin's wife Mehitable was her father's sister, so the two families were twice joined. Through this descent Keturah is the bridge between John's Pennsylvania ancestors and the colonial Tuthill and Smith families of Long Island.

About 1770, in Orange County, she married Thomas Lamoreaux, who served as ensign in the Woodbury Clove and Upper Clove militia companies commanded by her uncles in 1775 and 1776; the 1775 Cornwall Precinct association list carries his name alongside those of her brothers James and John. The marriage was probably by banns. In 1790 she moved with her husband to Plymouth in Luzerne County, Pennsylvania, and later to Jackson Township. In August 1812 she and Thomas sold their son John the homestead lots at Plymouth, 103 acres from Thomas's Pennsylvania patent; Keturah signed the deed with her mark. Thomas's will left her "my best horse saddle & bridle" and one hundred dollars.

Keturah died on 10 March 1833 at Plymouth, in the part that later became Jackson Township, "without a struggle or a groan". The Republican Farmer of Wilkes-Barre remembered her as one of the earliest settlers of Plymouth, who had raised thirteen children and lived to see 97 grandchildren and 114 great-grandchildren. She was buried in the Lamoreaux Family Burying Ground there. A death date of 1842 sometimes given for her belongs to her daughter Keturah. She was John's 6th-great-grandmother.

researchNotes:
Keturah Tuttle was born in Dec 1755 at Woodbury Clove, Orange Co., NY (SAR application ACN 58344 gives 1755 at 'Woodbury Clove', matching Alva Tuttle). She was probably a daughter of John Tuthill (c.1730-c.1770) and Temperance Smith (Alva Tuttle, Tuttle-Tuthill Lines, 1968, p.311: children twins James & John 1753, twins Ezekiel & William c.1754, Keturah ~1755, Samuel and Daniel); her children's names James, Temperance and Keturah follow that family. Her uncles Capt. Francis Smith and Capt. Austin Smith commanded the Woodbury Clove and Upper Clove militia companies in 1775-76, with her husband as ensign. She married Thomas Lamoreaux and moved with him to Plymouth (1790) and Jackson Twp. His will left her 'my best horse saddle & bridle' and $100. She died 10 Mar 1833 (obituary, Republican Farmer, Wilkes-Barre, 13 Mar 1833; WikiTree Tuthill-530; Find a Grave 269816651, Lamoreaux Family Burying Ground, Jackson Twp). The tree's death of 1842 (tree shows 1755-1842) is her daughter Keturah's (Harvey Book p.360). (Her Tuttle/Smith ancestors are covered in the colonial section.)

No record found this round names Keturah's parents directly, so her parentage stays probable. New circumstantial support: the 1775 Cornwall Precinct association list carries both 'James Tuttle' and 'John Tuthill' as well as her husband Thomas Lamoureux ([R4-S3]). On Alva Tuttle's reconstruction these are her twin brothers James and John (b. 1753). Her mother Temperance Smith's place in the family of James Smith & Jerusha Topping is now backed by two independent printed authorities: Pelletreau (1898) and C. H. Weygant's Family Record (1897), which names James and Jerusha's daughters Eunice, Keturah, Temperance and Jerusha and puts Capt. Austin and Capt. Francis Smith, their sons, at Woodbury Clove 'some twenty years or more' before the Revolution ([R4-S1], [R4-S2]). Keturah was evidently named for her aunt Keturah Smith.

The printed list of pre-1784 New York marriage licenses has no Lamoreaux-Tuthill (or Tuthill-Smith) entry, so these marriages were probably by banns ([R4-S4]).

Alva Tuttle (1968), p. 356: 'KETURAH TUTHILL c1755 Orange Co,NY da John c1730 & Temp SMITH; liv 1816 Luzerne Co,Pa; m Orange Co,NY Thos d 1829 Luzerne Co,Pa s John & Charity (DAVENPORT) LAMOREAUX  LTV', followed by thirteen children: Martha c1775 m Saml Pringle; Eliz 30 Sep 1776 m Geo Palmer Ransom; Jas m Sarah Hunter, 10 ch; Danl m Martha Linn; John 21 Nov 1780, unm; Charity m Peter Steele; Hannah m Stpn Van Loon; Thos 19 Aug 1787 m Mary Boston; Amelia m Fletcher Case; Keturah 18 Feb 1791 m Saml Ackley; Jane m Absalom Case; Temp m Matthias Van Loon; Josh 30 Aug 1799 m Betty Ives. The source code LTV is Lotta (Tuthill) Vail, a contributing compiler born 7 Sep 1880 (List of Contributing Compilers): Alva credits her, not a primary record, for the whole Tuthill–Smith–Lamoreaux family.

Round of 20 Oct–15 Nov 2026 (uploaded notes and the 'Bull Smith and Matt Damon' report). (1) The marriage of her parents is now primary: Rev. Napthali Daggett's Smithtown Presbyterian register, 'Nov. 23. John Tuthill & Temperance Smith, 8/.' (NYGBR 44:283; Robbins compared it with Dexter's 1899 certified copy at Yale). Ancestry's 'NYC Compiled Marriage Index' p. 283 is this same printed page. The register also has Zebulon Smith (Temperance's brother) & Elizabeth Green, 26 Mar 1752. (2) F. K. Smith (1967) no. 102: 'Austin, m. Mehitable Tuthill' (daughter of James Tuthill of Fireplace); no. 107: 'Temperance, supposed to have m. John Tuthill, brother of above Mehitable'. Lotta Vail appears among his authorities too, so F. K. Smith and Alva Tuttle are not fully independent. (3) The earliest statement of her maiden name is the 1885 DeKalb County history (p. 882, Chester P. Hodge), which also places her Tuttle kin in Orange County; the 1919 Lamoureux record agrees. (4) Three DAR GRC lineage sheets (image groups 008978799 img 331 and 008978866 img 616, and National No. 275101) give the marriage ca. 1770 in Orange County, Keturah 'living 4/16/1816' (Alva's 'liv 1816', which SAR files turned into a death year), and the headstone erected by a local chapter of the Daughters of 1812. None names her parents. (5) Luzerne Deed Book 105 pp. 266–268: Thomas and 'Keturah his wife' sold Lot 28 and the east half of Lot 30 (Plymouth, fourth division) to John Lamoreaux, 22 Aug 1812, for $266.67; the land came from Thomas's own PA patent of 18 May 1812, so it says nothing of Tuthill land. Witnesses Jesse Fell and James Lamoreaux for Thomas, Joshua and Daniel Lamoreaux for Keturah, who signed by mark and was examined separately before Jacob J. Bogardus on 21 Feb 1817; recorded 30 Oct 1865. Related deeds: 10 Oct 1798 Jehiel Fuller to James Lamoreaux Jr. (Lot 34); 10 Mar 1800 George P. Ransom to Thomas, a third of Lot 30 (image group 008086454, img 414); 1861 John Steel deed reciting an 1833 deed from Peter Steel and Charity his wife (008086639, img 503). (6) The Orange County grantor index T 1765–1828 has no deed by John (c.1730), Temperance or Keturah; leads are Daniel Tuthill & wife to Timothy Scidmore (c.1802, Liber H p. 214) and John Tuthill, wife Melicent and others to Daniel Tuthill Jr. (1819, Liber T p. 473), possibly a heirs' deed. (7) Lotta (Tuthill) Vail (b. 1880), Alva's source 'LTV', was researching the family from about 1916 (NYGBR queries 50:89, 50:299, 51:94) from Detroit and later Michigan City, Indiana; her papers have not been found (ask the Burton Historical Collection, Detroit Public Library; Michigan City Public Library; NYG&B). Rival Keturahs: Keturah Tuthill who married John Johnson Jr. at Rome, NY in 1832 and Keturah Tuttle Platt (d. 1850, Whippany NJ, b. c.1764) are different women. Overall Keturah link about 80%.
